outputs: SHIPPED — PostFX.js `_passGodRays`: uDecay is now anchored to GOD_SAMPLES (Math.pow(0.94, 24 / this._godSamples)). The decay-weighted tap count (1-d^N)/(1-d) was 12.89/14.37/15.81 against a 1/N normalisation, so the same scene emitted 1.612/1.347/0.988 times the marched radiance at MEDIUM/HIGH/ULTRA — desktop, the showcase tier, was rendering the shafts 39% dimmer than the phone. Now 1.612/1.599/1.587. At 24 taps the expression is exactly 0.94, so the phone MEDIUM review set is unchanged by this line by construction.

SHIPPED — PostFX.js FRAG_GOD_OCCLUSION: the sky-test comment corrected against a live readback of camera.far = 6200 (Terrain.js:603 raises it from Engine's authored 900). The 0.70/0.92 linear band is 4340-5704 m, not the 630-828 m the comment reasoned about; the test only still works because Sky.js's dome is depthWrite:false and leaves the cleared depth of 1.0.

DISPROOF — the sun pose is not the fault and HANDOFF open item 11 is STALE. Live on the sun beat, PostFX._sunUv = (0.60509, 0.54474) and _sunScreenStrength = 1.0 (full gain, uGodStrength 0.80). Cinematic.js's current SHOTS.sun (pos [-4.4,1.0,36.9]) already documents the disc landing at UV (0.605,0.455), and the r15 critic measured it at (1529,530) px = (0.604,0.453) top-down. All three agree. The disc does NOT land on the shimenawa tassel; item 11's (0.500,0.500) describes a pose that was replaced. Close item 11.

DISPROOF — the emitter is not empty. Read back from rtGodA (337x156 at MEDIUM): 10.2-11.0% of texels non-zero across five variants, max channel-mean 0.998, p99 0.479. The zero region is exactly the depth-masked near geometry — the torii uprights, shimenawa, shide and bamboo are present as occluders. No gain change is needed to put occluders into the buffer; they are already there.

MEASURED — the pass emits a veil, not shafts. rtGodA is non-zero on ~10% of texels; rtGodB (the marched result) is non-zero on 99.9% of them, mean 0.1194, p50 0.0551, p90 0.2928, p99 0.9319. The march spreads a 10%-coverage emitter over the whole frame. That common-mode term is what the sky owner's ablation independently measured as the mid-field wash.

MEASURED — the march is converged and undersampling is NOT the limiter. Holding the gain (uDecay = 0.94^(24/N)), rtGodB mean/p90 go 0.1194/0.2928 at N=24, 0.1088/0.2703 at N=48 (-8.9%/-7.7%), 0.1083/0.2740 at N=96 (a further -0.5%/+1.4%). So 24 taps under-captures occlusion by ~8% of the marched radiance and 48 taps is converged to within 0.5%. Halving the step again buys nothing. Do not spend fill on GOD_SAMPLES for this finding.

DISPROOF (source-level) — PostFX is NOT the second multiplication in HANDOFF open item 2. FRAG_RESOLVE receives one colour input, tScene, the composited scene radiance; there is no indirect-only buffer for it to scale. `c *= occTint * k` is a per-pixel scalar multiply applied to key and fill alike, so it is hue-preserving; its only colour term, uAoTint (0.78,0.85,1.0), has B/R 1.282 and can therefore only make occluded pixels COOLER. Open item 2's premise that PostFX.js:397 'scales indirectDiffuse and not the key' is wrong at source. Materials.js:2237 is the sole surviving named suspect.

DISPROOF (analytic) — the shadow-temperature target is unreachable from PostFX. Taking hero box (760,515,127,47) from B/R 0.579 to the critic's 1.30 requires blue to rise from display code 27.6 to 62 in a box whose red is 47.7. The only shadow-selective additive term in this file is uLift (currently 0.0240,0.0276,0.0372, already cool-weighted 1:1.15:1.55); the required increment is roughly +30 code values of blue on every pixel of every frame, against a black gate of p0.1 < 15 that currently reads 0/12/0/1/6. Every other shadow-selective term here is already cool: uAoTint, uVignetteTint (0.72,0.80,0.95), LOOK_MAGIC_HOUR shadowTint (0.130,0.152,0.185) and satShadow 0.86. The finding belongs upstream, where the critic routed it.

APPARATUS DISPROOF — the god-ray finding's acceptance metric cannot be satisfied by the effect it demands. `detail` is mean |Laplacian| per pixel, which for a sinusoid of amplitude A and wavelength L px returns 2A(1-cos(2pi/L))(2/pi). Measured with probe.mjs on synthetic strips: +/-40 code values at 60 px period scores detail 0.47, +/-25 at 60 px scores 0.47, +/-10 at 60 px scores 0.47 — all BELOW the 0.57 the critic called 'a mathematically smooth gradient', and level with the clean-sky control's 0.46. Only +/-25 at a 12 px period reaches 4.33, and that is grain, not a crepuscular shaft. An owner chasing detail >= 3.0 in that strip would be driven to add high-frequency noise.

APPARATUS FAULT (twice) — no pixel evidence was obtained. Run 1's screenshots were taken after engine.stop(); Engine constructs the renderer with preserveDrawingBuffer:false, so the composited buffer is already gone (98.7% of hero-base below code 16). This also means capture.mjs's --ab-object path, which screenshots in a separate round trip after engine.stop(), returns black A/B pairs. Run 2 kept the engine live but every frame carried the 陽炎 title card over an ink wash (95.5% below code 16, and h0-base / h1-ao0 / h2-aoback byte-identical). Probable cause: menus.skipIntro() was issued in the SAME page.evaluate as `void window.__kagerouStart()`, which is main.js's async begin(); capture.mjs only avoids this by using two separate evaluates. A corrected, guarded harness (it screenshots and checks luma p50 before spending evidence shots) is at scratchpad/pfx-abl3.mjs and was NOT run — the two-run budget was spent.
